clue.text: Chinese ruler, one requiring something to deal with the insects

definitions.text: something to deal with the insects

parts.note: Ch. is the abbreviation for Chinese
a lord is one who rules
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A Chinese emperor needs some remedy to cope with an insect plague.
explanation.definitionFit: Chlordan (also chlordane) is a chlorinated insecticide, a chemical for killing insects.

clue.text: Following misguided path, crass walker becomes low on funds

indicators.note: something misguided has gone astray, so the letters wander out of their order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange
ped is short for pedestrian, one who walks

explanation.surface: A boorish rambler who has taken a wrong turning ends up short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' tells you the walker comes after the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash-strapped is an idiom for being short of money, which is being low on funds.

clue.text: Bodily deficiency, advanced, more diseased, we heah?

indicators.note: the question about what we hear, spelt with a dropped r, signals a sound-alike in a non-rhotic accent

parts.note: high can mean advanced, as in high summer or a high level
poxier means more afflicted with the pox

explanation.surface: A medical note listing an advanced, worsening deficiency, read out in a drawling accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Said with the final r dropped, as the spelling 'heah' imitates, high poxier sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypoxia is a shortage of oxygen reaching the body's tissues, a physiological deficiency.

clue.text: Portly actor once losing weight? He's good fun

definitions.note: 'a laugh' is said of a person: 'he's a laugh'

indicators.note: losing means a part of the actor's surname is dropped

parts.note: Charles Laughton, the heavily built British-American film actor
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A stout actor of old slims down and asks whether he is now more entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the ton off Laughton leaves the answer; the question mark plays on the actor losing weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a laugh is colloquial for saying they are amusing company.

clue.text: Knight errant abroad discarding extremes of household chore?

indicators.note: discarding means some letters are thrown away from the chore

parts.note: ironing is a typical household chore

indicators.note: extremes are the outermost ends of a word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the chore are the ones dropped

explanation.surface: A wandering knight overseas gives up a dull domestic task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' marks the definition as foreign: the answer is Japanese.
explanation.definitionFit: A ronin was a masterless samurai in feudal Japan who roamed seeking service, a Japanese counterpart of the knight errant.

clue.text: Chaperones not available among cavorting nudes

indicators.note: among places one piece in the middle of the other
cavorting is leaping about, so the letters jump into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
n/a is the standard abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: Chaperones are nowhere to be found while naked people frolic.
explanation.definitionFit: Duennas are older women who supervise young girls, especially in Spain, acting as chaperones.

clue.text: E.g. Sumatran on site, working

indicators.note: working suggests something being worked over into a new form

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man from Sumatra is on the building site, doing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A nesiot is an islander; someone from the island of Sumatra is an example.

clue.text: A tangle? Net's there in one with it

indicators.note: a tangle is a muddled snarl, so the letters around it are jumbled
saying one word is there together with the solution means it must be taken back out of the jumble

parts.note: the phrase itself supplies the letters
these letters are found within the jumble together with the answer

explanation.surface: A knotted mess of netting, with seaweed snarled in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite clue: the letters of A TANGLE are the answer together with NET, so take NET out and rearrange what is left. 'A tangle' does double duty as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangle is a name for large brown seaweeds such as oarweed, and a seaweed is an alga.

clue.text: Reject as spurious amateur article about position coming up

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for amateur

indicators.note: about means going round, so the article encloses the other piece

parts.note: the definite article

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a site is a position or location

explanation.surface: A dabbler's paper is dismissed as fake because of a rising career post.
explanation.definitionFit: To athetise is a scholarly term for marking a passage as not genuine, rejecting it as spurious.

clue.text: Old clothes lined with wool left by court maiden long ago

indicators.note: something lined with a material has it on the inside

parts.note: gere is an old spelling of gear, meaning clothing

indicators.note: what is left once one part departs is the remainder after that part is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
to woo is to court

explanation.surface: Antique garments lined with wool were bequeathed by a lady of the royal court long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left by' works on wool: what wool leaves once the courting verb departs is a single letter. 'Old' tells you the clothing word is in an archaic spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerle is an obsolete spelling of girl, so it means a maiden in old texts.

clue.text: A magic mantra when this is this

definitions.text: A magic mantra when this is this

indicators.note: the answer describes the relationship between the phrase and itself, so the phrase must be a rearranged form of the answer

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A riddle about a magic incantation that is somehow equal to itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue says: A MAGIC MANTRA is anagrammatic of the answer, and the answer is anagrammatic of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anagrammatic describes letters forming an anagram of another word or phrase, which these two phrases are of each other.

clue.text: No serious affair, a tiny thing involving what's true but unsteady

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a mote is a tiny speck

indicators.note: unsteady means wobbling and unsettled, so the letters do not stay in place

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A light romance can be sincere yet still shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: An amourette is a brief, trifling love affair, the opposite of a serious one.

clue.text: Is leaving some Bantus for piecework?

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun, tuts being jobs of piecework

indicators.note: leaving means the named letters walk out of the word

parts.note: the Tutsi are a Bantu-speaking people of Rwanda and Burundi
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether some African workers are paid by the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A tut, as in tut-work, is a mining and dialect word for work paid by the piece or job.

clue.text: The old succumb to sea-sickness? Sailors on board hasten as before

indicators.note: on board means inside the vessel, so one piece is carried within the other

parts.note: spue is an old spelling of spew, to vomit
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Seasick sailors on a ship hurry to the rail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea-sickness' and 'Sailors on board' paint one scene, but only the spelling of the vomiting word is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurne is a Spenserian form of spur, an archaic verb meaning to hurry or press on.

clue.text: A traditional Afghan council requiring day of fasting locally?

parts.note: taken as written
a shura is a consultative council of elders in Afghanistan

explanation.surface: An Afghan tribal council calls for a day of fasting in the region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' points to the same Muslim setting as the council.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashura is the tenth day of Muharram, a Muslim fast day and day of mourning for Shia.

clue.text: Wells maybe the sea breaks into, yielding fine gravel

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: H. G. Wells, the novelist, known by his initials
the oggin is naval slang for the sea

explanation.surface: Coastal wells are flooded when the sea gets in, leaving behind fine gravel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wells' looks like water sources by the sea; it is the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogging (or hoggin) is a mixture of fine gravel, sand and clay used for paths.

clue.text: Sun brings in melting of ice and cheers of community

indicators.note: bringing something in puts it inside

parts.note: Sol is the sun

indicators.note: melting changes the shape of something, so the letters lose their form

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: Sunshine melts the ice and the whole neighbourhood cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: Societal means relating to society, so it is an adjective for something of the community.

clue.text: Big win at the pokies? Second with reserve fund backed

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so these letters run from right to left

parts.note: the rest is a bank's reserve fund

explanation.surface: A gambler wins big on the slot machines and banks the takings as savings.
explanation.walkthrough: Pokies are Australian slot machines; the answer is Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A motser is Australian slang for a large sum of money, especially a gambling win.

clue.text: Recording system for capturing 'fab' number?

indicators.note: capturing means taking hold of, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: to can stand for for, as in a toast to someone
the Beatles were the Fab Four, and four is IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A video recorder set to tape a Beatles hit.
explanation.definitionFit: TiVo is a brand of digital video recorder, a system for recording television.

clue.text: What can be mistaken for this American forest? Taiga can

indicators.note: being mistaken for something else means appearing in a muddled form

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Could a northern forest be confused with a South American one? It can.
explanation.walkthrough: Taiga is the northern conifer forest, so it looks like part of the definition, but it is the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Caatinga is the thorny scrub forest of north-eastern Brazil, a forest of South America.

clue.text: A drug I take internally dispersed pains

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so two pieces go within the scattered letters
dispersed means scattered about, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
taken as written
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Someone takes a painkiller to make their aches go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkilling drug, acetylsalicylic acid.

clue.text: Seating arranged to display shrub

indicators.note: arranged means put in a chosen order, here a different one

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Garden chairs are set out so as to show off a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Genista is a genus of broom shrubs with yellow pea-like flowers.

clue.text: Spiny creature nipping booby in swimming races

indicators.note: nipping means grasping, so the jumbled letters clasp the other piece
swimming suggests something moving about, so the letters float out of order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
a booby is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A prickly sea creature bites a seabird during swimming races.
explanation.walkthrough: A booby is also a seabird, which suits the surface, but here it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The rascasse is the scorpionfish, a spiny Mediterranean fish used in bouillabaisse.

clue.text: The old take possession of space in front of church

parts.note: an area is a space
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Elderly people occupy the open ground before a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks the definition as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Areach is an obsolete verb meaning to seize or reach out and take.

clue.text: Look concealed by those embarrassed

indicators.note: concealed by means kept out of sight inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: People who feel ashamed hide their expression.
explanation.definitionFit: To look and to seem are synonyms as verbs: to appear to be.

clue.text: Wannabes do (a father taking lead in publicity)

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: taking means accepting inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a sire is a father

indicators.note: the lead of a word is the letter that goes first

parts.note: the first letter of publicity

explanation.surface: Would-be celebrities perform, with a dad in charge of their promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sentence: wannabes are people who aspire, so 'Wannabes do' means what they do.
explanation.definitionFit: Wannabes are people who hope to become something, which is to say they have ambitions.

clue.text: Tardigrade mammal, one of deadly group

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a slow-moving tree-dwelling mammal; tardigrade means slow-paced
second meaning: one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.walkthrough: Tardigrade here is the adjective meaning slow-stepping, not the microscopic water bear.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloth is a slow-moving mammal, and sloth, meaning laziness, is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: What Scots have for breakfast, losing itch for fry, singularly?

indicators.note: losing means some letters are lost from the dish

parts.note: parritch is the Scots word for porridge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scottish breakfast question about whether a fried dish can stop you scratching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fry' means young fish, and 'singularly' asks for one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A parr is a young salmon, and fry are young fish, so one of the fry.

clue.text: What's in a steak? Bit of brisket has all-round quality

indicators.note: having something all round means being surrounded by it

parts.note: tone is a quality, as of sound or character

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a single letter, here its first

parts.note: the first letter of brisket

explanation.surface: A butcher's question about a cut of beef that is good all over.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the T-shaped bone found in a T-bone steak.
explanation.definitionFit: The T-bone is the bone in a cut of sirloin steak, which also names the steak.

clue.text: After time Muscovite maybe is seen to pack up

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a Russ is a Russian, and a Muscovite is an example

explanation.surface: A Moscow resident is seen to pack their bags after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the Russian follows the time.
explanation.definitionFit: To truss is to tie up or bundle tightly, packing something up.

clue.text: Nigerian king has foreign company protecting church vessels

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding something to guard it

parts.note: Cia is the abbreviation for company in Spanish and Portuguese
the Ibo (Igbo) are a people of Nigeria
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An African monarch has an overseas firm guarding vessels in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nigerian king' looks like one thing but is two: the people and the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciboria are covered chalices used to hold the consecrated bread in church.

clue.text: Pastor distributed ancient service book

indicators.note: distributed means shared out and scattered, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A minister hands out an old prayer book.
explanation.definitionFit: A portas is an old name for a portable breviary, a book of church services.

clue.text: Vigorous

clue.text: Spiny fish 'urts badly — feelin' pain inside

clue.text: Part of bee's anatomy: one's achy when it's deployed
